subject: Portside: 2027 renewal — credit & commit discussion
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Ng <laura@portside.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Portside: 2027 renewal — credit & commit discussion

Hi Laura —

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. Per our notes, Portside is looking to renew for calendar 2027 and consolidate two smaller commits into a single annual committed volume. The quick proposal from my side:

- Consolidate Q2/Q3 commitments into a 12‑month anchored commit (covers compute + inference tokens).
- Apply an anchored credit of 10% of the annual committed spend to smooth the transition (one‑time credit applied at PO).
- Hold current per-token rates for 12 months from the renewal effective date (price‑hold).
- Add a modest burst pool for 15% over commit with tiered overage pricing.

I've attached a term sheet draft and a usage file we pulled for Q1 to help size things. If this structure looks reasonable, we can bake it into a formal SOW and route through procurement.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm the target annual commit range (ballpark is fine).
2) We agree on the credit structure and effective date.
3) We circulate a redlineable term sheet to your contracts team.

Attached: Portside_Renewal_Term_Sheet_v3.pdf (term sheet draft), usage_breakdown_Q1-2027.csv

Thanks — happy to hop on 30m if helpful.

Best,
Priyom
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
pri@redwood.ai

From: Laura Ng <laura@portside.ai>

Cc: Ethan Russo <ethan.russo@portside.ai>, contracts@portside.ai
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Portside: 2027 renewal — credit & commit discussion

Priyom —

Thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifying items from our side:

- Can you confirm whether the anchored credit is refundable if we downsize mid‑year?
- The burst pool sounds good; we need the overage tiers spelled out (we typically do 0–15%, 15–50%, 50%+ buckets).
- Our procurement lead (contracts@portside.ai) will want the exact rate hold language and the definition of "effective date."

I'm attaching our internal Q1 runtimes and a projected growth curve for FY27 — helps explain why we want a single consolidated commit.

If you can sketch pricing for three commit bands (Base: $250k, Mid: $500k, Stretch: $900k annual spend) with the credit and hold applied, that will help us present to finance next week.

Appreciate it — Laura
VP Product, Portside Logistics
[Attachment: portside_Q1_runtimes.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

Hi Laura / team —

Following up with a concise set of pricing sketches for the three bands you requested. These are indicative and assume a 12‑month commitment with the 10% anchored credit applied at signing. All rates in $ per 1k tokens (effective per-token rate after credit applied across the annual usage estimate):

- Base (250k annual spend): $4.60 / 1k tokens, burst tiers: 0–15% @ +12%, 15–50% @ +28%, 50%+ @ +55%
- Mid (500k): $3.95 / 1k tokens, burst tiers: 0–15% @ +10%, 15–50% @ +25%, 50%+ @ +50%
- Stretch (900k): $3.35 / 1k tokens, burst tiers: 0–15% @ +8%, 15–50% @ +20%, 50%+ @ +45%

Key commercial notes:
- The anchored credit (10%) is a one‑time contra applied to the first invoice; it is non‑refundable if Portside elects to downsize mid‑term, but we can discuss prorating for material reductions with advance notice.
- Price hold applies to the SKU/rate for 12 months from the effective date and excludes any third‑party hardware pass‑throughs.
- We can include a true‑up at year‑end if actual usage exceeds the committed band by >25% (standard true‑up math).

I've attached a quick term sheet with the numeric examples called Portside_Renewal_Term_Sheet_v3.pdf (version with rates). Happy to jump on a call to walk through the bands.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Portside_Renewal_Term_Sheet_v3.pdf (pdf)]

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Portside renewal commercial exception request

Vivek / Marissa —

Quick ask: Portside has signaled a strong preference for the Mid band but expects to grow toward Stretch within 9–12 months. To win the renewal and secure the upsell runway, I recommend we offer the 10% anchored credit (one‑time) and confirm a 12‑month price hold, but add an internal concession: allow a pro‑rated refund of the anchored credit if Portside increases commit to Stretch within 6 months (effectively converting the credit into a pre‑paid commitment balance).

Rationale: This is higher short‑term cost to Redwood (credit refund clause) but materially increases the probability of upsell and long term ARR (Portside is strategically aligned and a good reference).

Risks / mitigations:
- Risk: Abuse (customer downsizes after receiving refund). Mitigation: refund only if increased commit is executed (contract sign), require 30 days notice, and cap refundable amount to 60% of the credit.
- Risk: Accounting complexity. Mitigation: route a written amendment that clearly moves the credit to a pre‑paid balance upon commit increase. Finance is OK with the flow if legal approves language.

If you approve, I'll send a revised term sheet to Contracts with the amendment language and run the PO timeline.

Thanks — Priyom

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Ng <laura@portside.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, contracts@portside.ai
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Portside: 2027 renewal — credit & commit discussion

Laura / Portside contracts team —

Good news: Redwood is prepared to move forward with the Mid band at the rates Ben outlined plus the 10% anchored credit. Per internal approval, we will include the conversion clause that allows Portside to convert the anchored credit into a pre‑paid commitment balance if you increase to the Stretch band within the first 6 months. Key points below for procurement: 

- Effective date: 2027‑06‑01 (start of new billing cycle).
- Price hold: 12 months from effective date; excludes third‑party pass‑throughs.
- Anchored credit: 10% applied to first invoice, convertible to pre‑paid balance upon signed amendment to Stretch commit (conversion capped at 60% refundable as pre‑paid credit).
- Burst pool: 15% free buffer, then tiered overage as outlined in Ben's note.
- Standard year‑end true‑up applies for >25% variance.

Attached is the updated term sheet for signature (Portside_Renewal_Term_Sheet_v3.pdf). Please route this to procurement and let me know the preferred DocuSign contact. If we can get signatures by 5/12, Legal will aim to return countersigned docs within 72 hours.

Next steps:
1) Contracts review and confirm DocuSign contact.
2) Procurement issues PO referencing DEAL ID PORT-2027-0123.
3) We schedule a kickoff week of 6/1 to align telemetry and onboarding.

Thanks — excited to keep building with Portside.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Lead | Redwood Inference
